_comment: Patterns and allowlists for the health rules (datapipeline/health.py): 0.1b's R1 to R8, and 0.1d's R9 to R14 for the 6 Oct 2026 corpus reviews. Keys under each rule name a collection, or "all". A P1 PR that changes what a rule should see edits this file, not the code.

R9_trailing_heading._comment: A passage, followed by another, whose last of two or more lines is under max_chars, starts with a capital and has no final punctuation: the next section's heading glued on (C-08, Opus A-003). A block rule in these collections since 1.3a.

R10_site_boilerplate._comment: Block rule. A website's own text inside a passage (C-05, Opus A-005, Opus-2 B-008), matched case-insensitively.

H7_unmarked_heading._comment: Block rules H7 and H8 (issue #445) run in these collections only, in `authors`' documents of a collection (Vatican II among the councils), and in the `documents` listed one at a time (new works in a collection whose others are not marked yet): a heading-like paragraph (headings.looks_like_heading) with no mark in metadata.headings, and a level-1 heading that opens its chapter and repeats the chapter label without chapter_title. A collection joins when its adapter marks its headings. not_headings lists, by document ID, paragraphs the classifier takes for headings that are text (a signature, a dating line, a quotation lead-in), each with its reason; they are matched without case or punctuation.

R11_papal_editorial._comment: An editor's or translator's words in a papal passage (C-18, Opus A-010); the last pattern is an "[N-M]" paragraph-range marker, which only a table of contents prints.

R12_note_caller._comment: A footnote caller left in the text (C-17): Opus A-012's "(N)"/"(N*)" after a word and a digit glued after punctuation, Opus-2 B-005's number after sentence punctuation and a space (not before a Bible book), and "[ N ]". not_after skips a match whose preceding 16 characters end like a Scripture citation ("Rom. i.", "3:16.") or a reference ("cf. 1 C,or. 3:7", a misprint in vatican.va's Ad Gentes 40, 1.1) or the bracketed volume of an Acta Apostolicae Sedis citation ("AAS [39] 1947", The Catholic Mind's Menti Nostrae, 1.3d). A bracketed verse range after a Bible chapter ("St. Luke writes in the second Chapter [21]", "Mark, Chapter 16 [9]": the Spiritual Exercises' Mysteries, 5.6b) is a citation. Summa brackets are summa_bracket_numbers'.

R13_lower_start._comment: Report only: a passage that starts with a lowercase letter (C-27, Opus A-018). No settings.

R14_hyphen_space._comment: Report only: a letter, a hyphen, a space and a lowercase letter, a word broken at a line end (C-16, Opus A-021, Sol A-010). The reviewed broken words are mended by normalize/broken_words.json (1.10a). allowed lists the reviewed forms that are not broken words, lowercased as matched: suspended hyphens ("short- and long-term"), the editors' spelling notes in Arnobius ("cog- for the ms."), which 1.10b strips with the other notes, and dashes the source prints as a hyphen and a space ("action- it has escaped").
